title: Was There Really a Female King in Ancient Egypt 5,000 Years Ago? - Nautilus
gist: Meretneith, a royal woman of Egypt's First Dynasty over 5,000 years ago and possibly daughter of King Djer, was buried with riches fit for a male ruler, implying she was at least an interim ruler or co-regent. Egyptologists have long disputed whether she ruled in her own right, a question that requires textual evidence naming her as ruler.
